about:
# FadeUI

Auto hide the World of Warcraft UI out of combat for a clean, immersive screen. Each
Blizzard element (action bars, player frame, minimap, chat...) can be shown **Always**,
**In combat**, **Combat/Target**, **Out of combat**, or **Never**, like pressing Alt-Z
but per element and automatic. Visibility is driven by secure state drivers, so
elements appear and disappear in combat without taint errors, and keybinds keep
working on hidden bars.

## Usage

- `/fadeui` or `/fui` — open the options window
- Keybindings → AddOns → FadeUI — toggle FadeUI (like Alt-Z) or open options
- Addon compartment (minimap) button — left-click toggles, right-click opens options

Drag the grip in the options window's bottom-right corner to make it bigger or smaller, from
75% to 150%, and double-click it to go back to 100%.

## Development

Addon source lives in `FadeUI/`. Link it into your WoW client so changes load on `/reload`:

```sh
scripts/link.sh                # _forever_ (default)
scripts/link.sh _retail_       # or any other flavor folder
```

Set `WOW_DIR` if WoW isn't installed at `/Applications/World of Warcraft` (macOS) or
`C:\Program Files (x86)\World of Warcraft` (Windows, given as WSL sees it, such as
`/mnt/d/Games/World of Warcraft`). On Windows, run it from WSL: the game can't follow a link
into WSL, so the script copies the folder instead. Run it again after each change, then
`/reload`. A copy it made has a `.copied-from` file in it, and is copied over the next time;
any other folder of that name is moved aside first, as on macOS.

To support another addon, add a file for it to `FadeUI/Addons/` and list it in
`FadeUI/Addons/Addons.xml`. `FadeUI/Addons.lua` describes what a file can declare, and
`Addons/Questie.lua` and `Addons/Chattynator.lua` are examples.

## Contributing

Report bugs and request features with the [issue forms](https://github.com/bstotmeister/fadeui/issues/new/choose).
For branches, pull requests, labels, milestones and releasing, see [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/bstotmeister/fadeui/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).

# FadeUI

## [v1.3.0](https://github.com/bstotmeister/fadeui/tree/v1.3.0) (2026-11-06)
[Full Changelog](https://github.com/bstotmeister/fadeui/compare/v1.2.0...v1.3.0) [Previous Releases](https://github.com/bstotmeister/fadeui/releases)

- Release v1.3.0: show action bars while dragging or in Quick Keybind Mode (#19)  
    ## What it does  
    - **Dragging:** while you hold a spell, item, macro or pet action on the  
    cursor, Action Bars 1–8 and the Pet Bar show, whatever their mode, so  
    you can drop it into a slot. They fade out again once you let go. A new  
    option, "Also show all action bars while you drag a spell or item" (on  
    by default), sits below the Pet Bar row.  
    - **Quick Keybind Mode:** while it's open, every action bar shows  
    (including the Stance Bar), so you can hover the buttons to bind them.  
    This works whether it's opened from Settings or Edit Mode. There's no  
    option for it.  
    Bars turned off in Edit Mode or Settings stay hidden in both cases.  
    ## How it works  
    - Both use the existing "peek" path that bag buttons use while bags are  
    open: `Holder_State` forces `"show"` for a holder whose element is being  
    peeked, and `UpdatePeek` re-checks it.  
    - Dragging is detected with `ACTIONBAR_SHOWGRID` / `ACTIONBAR_HIDEGRID`  
    and `PET_BAR_SHOWGRID` / `PET_BAR_HIDEGRID`, the same events that show  
    empty slot grids.  
    - Quick Keybind Mode is detected by hooking `QuickKeybindFrame`  
    OnShow/OnHide. Blizzard's `QuickKeybindFrame.QuickKeybindModeEnabled`  
    callback is registered for but never fired in the current UI source, so  
    it can't be used.  
    - New element fields: `drag` (bars you can drop onto) and `bar` (every  
    element in the Action bars group, set from `bars = true` on the group).  
    ## Testing  
    - `luacheck FadeUI` passes.  
    - Not yet tested in game. To check: set the bars to "Never", then drag a  
    spell, an item, a macro and a pet ability; untick the option and drag  
    again; open Quick Keybind Mode from Settings and from Edit Mode.  
    ## Version  
    - `## Version` in `FadeUI.toc`: 1.2.0 → 1.3.0.  
    ## Notes  
    - Neither works in combat: action bar holders are secure and can't be  
    shown mid-fight (bag buttons have the same limit). A drag that ends in  
    combat hides its bars when combat ends.  
    🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)  
    ---------  
    Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Adds a line about the spell helper icon, a "Why FadeUI" section, and keyword-friendly section headings. Feature details are unchanged.

# FadeUI

## [v1.2.0](https://github.com/bstotmeister/fadeui/tree/v1.2.0) (2026-11-05)
[Full Changelog](https://github.com/bstotmeister/fadeui/compare/v1.1.0...v1.2.0) [Previous Releases](https://github.com/bstotmeister/fadeui/releases)

- Release v1.2.0: minimap styles, spell helpers, options search (#17)  
    ## Summary  
    Version 1.2.0, with everything merged since 1.1.0:  
    - **Minimap styles (#13, #16):**  
    - While shown: Normal, or Map (no border or buttons, cropped to a circle  
    at your usual zoom, 30% to 100%).  
    - While hidden: None, Nodes (only herb and ore nodes, quest areas, party  
    members and your arrow), or Map.  
    - Hover a node or marker to see what it is. Clicking the map pings, with  
    an option to make clicks go through instead.  
    - **Spell helpers (#9, #14, #15):** when a spell fails because you're  
    out of range, short on resource or it's on cooldown, its icon shows  
    until it's ready. `/fui range` moves the icon.  
    - **Options search (#10):** filter the element list by name.  
    - **Bag buttons (#11):** can also show while your bags are open.  
    ## This PR  
    - `## Version` in `FadeUI.toc`: 1.1.0 → 1.2.0.  
    - `docs/curseforge-description.md`: adds Minimap styles and Spell  
    helpers sections, plus the search box, bag buttons and `/fui range`.  
    ## Release steps after merge  
    Tag `v1.2.0` on the merge commit and push it; CI creates the GitHub  
    release. Then run `scripts/release.sh` locally from the tag to upload to  
    CurseForge. A dry run of the packager on this branch includes all 14  
    minimap masks and leaves out `scripts/`.  
    🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)  
    Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Minimap: hover tooltips and click-to-ping in Nodes and Map (#16)  
    ## What it does  
    - **Tooltips:** in the Nodes and Map minimap styles, hovering a node, quest marker or party member shows its tooltip again, the same as on the normal minimap.  
    - **Pinging:** a new "Click the map to ping" option (on by default, at the end of the "Minimap when shown" row). On, clicking the map pings that spot for your group. Off, clicks go through to the world.  
    ## How it works  
    - While the minimap is moved out of its cluster, it always responds to mouse-over (`SetMouseMotionEnabled(true)`). It responds to clicks only with ping on (`SetMouseClickEnabled`). Before, its mouse was turned off completely.  
    - A cropped map (below 100%) only takes the mouse within the square around its circle (`SetHitRectInsets`). The empty area further out passes everything through.  
    - When the minimap returns to normal, its original click, mouse-over and hit-area settings are put back.  
    - The option dims unless one of the rows uses Map or Nodes.  
    ## Testing  
    - `luacheck FadeUI` passes.  
    - Tested in game: tooltips show in Nodes and Map, pinging works, and with ping off, clicks go through.  
    ## Notes  
    - While the cursor is over the map area, things in the world behind it don't get mouse-over, the same as with the normal minimap.  
    - With ping on in Nodes, the invisible full-size minimap area catches clicks.  
    - On a cropped map, a click in a corner just outside the circle can still ping a spot beyond the visible map.  
    🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)  
- Cooldown helper: ignore a spell's cooldown right after you cast it (#15)  
    ## Summary  
    - **Problem:** pressing a spell again straight after casting it (e.g. spamming Charge on a warrior) fails with "not ready", which brought up the cooldown helper's icon while you were still pressing the button.  
    - **Cooldown buffer:** a spell failing on cooldown within this many seconds of you casting it is now ignored. It applies only to that spell and only to cooldown failures; range and resource failures still show straight away.  
    - **Options:** a **Buffer** seconds box on a new line under the Cooldown helper's seconds (2s by default; 0 = off, so every cooldown failure shows). It's dimmed while the Cooldown helper is off. It follows account-wide or per-character settings, and Reset to defaults resets it.  
    - The new line moves the minimap rows and element list down by one row.  
    ## Testing  
    - `luacheck FadeUI`: 0 warnings.  
    - In game: spamming Charge no longer brings up the icon (tested with the 2s buffer).  
    ## Not covered  
    - **Secret spell IDs:** if the game hides the spell ID of your cast (a secret value), the buffer can't tell which spell it was, so it doesn't apply.  
    🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)  
- Cooldown helper: show a spell's icon and cooldown when it fails on cooldown (#14)  
    ## Summary  
    - **Cooldown on the helper icon:** with the action bars hidden there was  
    no way to see a spell's cooldown. The range/resource helper icon now  
    shows it the way the action bars do: the sweep, the game's own countdown  
    numbers (they follow the game's "show cooldown numbers" setting) and the  
    bling when it ends.  
    - **Cooldown helper:** when a spell fails because it isn't ready ("Spell  
    is not ready yet." / "Ability is not ready yet."), the helper icon  
    appears with that spell's cooldown. It works like the other two helpers:  
    it stays up while you tab targets, and hides when you cast the spell or  
    after its seconds.  
    - **Options:** a third **Cooldown helper** checkbox with its own seconds  
    box, next to Range and Resource (on, 8s by default; 0 = until you cast  
    the spell). It follows account-wide or per-character settings, and Reset  
    to defaults resets it.  
    - **Sweep follows the checkbox:** the sweep shows only while the  
    Cooldown helper is on, on range and resource icons too. This matches the  
    others: range is the border, resource is the icon, cooldown is the  
    sweep, and each shows only while its helper is on.  
    - **No early flash:** an icon shown for a cooldown doesn't do the  
    "ready" flash right away; the cooldown's bling marks when it's ready.  
    - **Secret values:** uses `C_Spell.GetSpellCooldownDuration` with  
    `SetCooldownFromDurationObject` when the client has them, since they  
    take secret values. Otherwise it uses `C_Spell.GetSpellCooldown`, and  
    shows no sweep if those values are secret.  
    - Dev: new error-string globals added to `.luacheckrc` and  
    `.vscode/settings.json`. `.vscode/settings.json` also picks up  
    `NUM_CONTAINER_FRAMES`, `MinimapCluster` and `HybridMinimap`, which were  
    already used in the code but missing from it.  
    ## Testing  
    - `luacheck FadeUI`: 0 warnings.  
    - Not yet tested in game: the cooldown sweep and numbers, the cooldown  
    helper's trigger, its seconds box, the sweep in combat (secret values)  
    and whether the options row still fits with three helpers.  
    ## Not covered  
    - **Charges:** spells with charges don't show their recharge the way the  
    action bars do.  
    - **Global cooldown:** pressing a spell again and again during the  
    global cooldown may bring up the icon with a "not ready" error. It hides  
    once that spell casts.  
    🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)  
    Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Minimap styles: nodes or a cropped map while hidden, and a map-only style while shown (#13)  
    ## What it does  
    With the minimap hidden, you lose herb and ore nodes, quest areas and party dots. This adds two rows in `/fui`:  
    ```  
    Minimap when shown:   [Normal] [Map]           Map size: [-] 100% [+]  
    Minimap when hidden:  [None] [Nodes] [Map]     Map size: [-]  50% [+]  
    ```  
    - **Nodes:** only what the minimap marks (herb and ore nodes, quest areas, party members, your arrow), with no map behind them.  
    - **Map:
